This cupboard is made of oak, yet this is entirely concealed beneath an expensive ebony veneer embellished with ivory. Even the interior of this painstakingly crafted cupboard is finished with exotic types of wood.

Around 1650, Antwerp was the leading centre of production for cabinets. They were made in large numbers and exported to many European countries. In general, they were richly and strikingly ornamented.
The back of the chair is heaving with richly carved decoration: interlaced strapwork with foliage and flowers, bunches of fruit, a cherub’s head and two lions bearing shields.
Large candlestands of this type served to support candelabra for three or more candles. They stood in the corners of sumptuously furnished interiors, or sometimes in larger series along galleries.

By shifting the back, you could use both sides of this settle. Sitting before a fire, you could alternate positions to keep your whole body warm. Under the seat is a storage space for keeping valuables safe.

This piece is a veritable princely art collection in miniature. All manner of materials and artefacts have been incorporated into it. Originally the many drawers and compartments contained works of art and natural specimens.
